ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all founders, protectors, beneficiaries, and foundation council members against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions, EU consolidated sanctions, Panama's national sanctioned-persons list, and PEP databases. Continuous monitoring is required under Ley No. 23 de 2015 and the rules of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Portal de Servicios Virtuales
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in Spanish or a Latin-script equivalent; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Spanish/Latin characters. Names must be distinct, not homonymous with existing registered companies, foundations, or other legal entities, and must not mislead the public.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a reconsideration request with the Registro Público de Panamá within five business days, providing evidence of distinctiveness and lawful use. If reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Dirección General del Registro Público within ten business days, followed by judicial appeal to the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within twenty business days. All filings must be made through the same virtual portal and require the applicant's digital signature and payment of the applicable fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are accepted only for registering the statutory agent and Panama registered office; a physical, non-virtual operational facility is required for any defense manufacturing activity, yet such facility is not permitted to be established under the private foundation vehicle itself and would need a separate Panamanian operational entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection by the UAF/FIU and the reinforced non-financial subject supervisor within the first 12 months is 85%, given the defense-tactical-hardware classification and high AML risk tier.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Private Interest Foundation Law (Ley No. 25 of 1995, as amended by Ley No. 59 of 2013), Articles 1-7 and 15-18; supplementary application of the Corporations Law (Ley General de Sociedades, Ley 32 de 1927) where the foundation charter adopts corporate governance rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) – Foundations Section (Vía España, Panama City), online filing via the official registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Private Instrument of Foundation (Instrumento Privado de Fundación) containing the foundation charter, endowment declaration, registered agent acceptance, and resolution of the initial Foundation Council, granted with notarial authentication.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The foundation charter must declare a minimum foundation capital of USD 10,000. No escrow or bank-deposit proof is required at filing; the capital may remain as a contingent endowment liability, and no mandatory paid-up certificate is submitted to the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a meeting of the Foundation Council duly convened and held, the following resolutions were adopted: (1) The subscription of the founding endowment for the Foundation’s tactical vehicle manufacturing activities is approved. (2) The registered office is fixed in Panama City, and the Resident Agent mandate is confirmed. (3) The appointment of the Foundation Council officers—President, Secretary, and Treasurer—is ratified, with authority to open bank accounts, execute government wire and diplomatic LC payments, and submit statutory license applications. (4) The industrial and environmental licensing steps are authorized. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Panamanian Resident Agent and Conduct AML/KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney acting as foundation Registered Agent (Resident Agent), approved to practice before the Public Registry of Panama.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The PIF founder signs a professional engagement agreement with a licensed Resident Agent. Submit corporate and beneficial-owner due diligence materials for Anti-Money-Laundering (AML) and Counter-Terrorist-Financing screening. The Agent confirms the exact foundation name, objects, governance structure, and registered office location to be inserted in the charter.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or national ID of founder and beneficial owner
Proof of corporate group structure and ultimate beneficial owner statement
Bank reference letter or source-of-funds declaration
Executed Resident Agent acceptance letter
AML/KYC questionnaire and sanctions-screen results
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Agent refuses engagement, the founder may appoint another licensed Resident Agent; any deficiency in KYC is cured by providing corrected due diligence forms and independent credit or legal reference notices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Foundation Charter and Endowment Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Civil Circuit (Notaría Pública del Circuito) of Panama City, in coordination with the foundation Resident Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Resident Agent prepares the private instrument in Spanish, setting out the foundation name, capital (USD 10,000), registered office, objects covering armored tactical vehicle manufacturing, Family/Protector Optional? The founder signs before the Notary, and the Notary authenticates the signature and protocolizes the instrument.
required_dossiers: Foundation charter draft approved by the Resident Agent
Endowment declaration stating the initial capital
Specific objects and powers including manufacturing, import/export, licensing, and bank account operations
Identification documents of the founder and initial Council members
Registered office acceptance by the Resident Agent
Payment receipt for notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies defects in the draft, the charter is redrafted at no substantial incremental cost and re-signed at a second notarial sitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Notarized Instrument to the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Foundations Section; official e-portal: imagenes.registropublico.gob.pa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Resident Agent or authorized counsel presents the notarized private instrument for registration. The Registry assigns a filing number, verifies the foundation name against prior registrations, examines the charter for legal compliance, and issues a preliminary qualification. Pay the registration fee and stamp taxes at the Registry cashier or through the online gateway.
required_dossiers: Notarized Private Instrument of Foundation (original and copies)
Certified copy of the notary’s protocol entry
Registry fee receipt
Founder and officer official IDs legalized as required
Certificate of Registered Agent acceptance (original)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an objection (nota), the Resident Agent files a correction memorial within the official calendar; if rejected a second time, an appeal is lodged before the Director General of the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certified Foundation Registration Certificate and Folio Record
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Foundations Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After final inscription, the foundation obtains a certified registration certificate (Certificado de Registro) and access to the folio number in the Foundation Book. The foundation is now a separate legal person with capacity to contract, open bank accounts, and own manufacturing assets. This certificate is the legal basis for applying for tax identification and industrial licenses.
required_dossiers: Application for certified certificate
Registry filing number and proof of payment of final fees
Legal representation or registered agent authorization letter
Company name and folio number if previously assigned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certified copy is delayed, the Resident Agent may request an expedited certification; if the folio contains errors, a corrective motion is made under Registry rules with supporting notarial correction instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Tax Authorities and Municipal Operations Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipality of Panama – Treasury and Business Licensing Department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the taxpayer identification number (RUC/Persona Jurídica), register as an industrial taxpayer, and apply for the municipal operating notice (Aviso de Operación). This step ensures the foundation can lawfully invoice, withhold taxes, and initiate the industrial license process for the tactical vehicle production plant.
required_dossiers: Certified foundation registration certificate from the Public Registry
Foundation charter showing industrial objects
Registered Agent and Council officers identification and authorization
Lease or ownership instrument for the registered office or plant site
DGI RUC application form
Municipal Aviso de Operación form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or Municipality queries the application, the registered agent cures the omission by submitting the requested notarized translation or supplementary balance sheet; administrative appeals proceed before the Fiscal Administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Directorate General of Industry and Business Development, Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI), together with the Ministry of Public Security for authorization of defense-related manufacturing activities under Panama’s arms-control rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operation License for Manufacturing of Armored Security and Tactical Personnel Transport Vehicles (Permiso de Operación Industrial), including a Special Authorization for Production of Restricted Military Materials under Decree Law 58 of 2007.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (MiAMBIENTE) – National Environmental Assessment Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Study (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental, Category II or III) required for motor-vehicle assembly, metal finishing, and painting operations; classification will be confirmed in the project’s terms of reference.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Panamanian Executive Decree No. 5 of 2009 and the National Effluent and Air Emission Rules: pH 6-9, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 200 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, hydrocarbons ≤ 15 mg/L, VOCs in paint booths treated and controlled below 50 mg/m3 as hourly average; hazardous waste must be managed under Law 5 of 1999, observing manifest and transport rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the National Civil Protection Service (SINAPROC) and the Panama Fire Department; structural load inspections of the assembly plant, paint-bay ventilation, and test-track surfaces certified by a licensed civil engineer; workplace hygiene and safety clearance issued by the Ministry of Health (MINSA) covering noise, industrial dust, ventilation, emergency exits, and personal protective equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); Sede Electrónica — https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) obtains its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) before the DGI. The procedure requires: (i) presentation of the foundation deed registered in the Registro Público de Panamá; (ii) notarized application identifying the resident agent and registered address; (iii) sworn declaration of any taxable activity; and (iv) issuance of the RUC and, where applicable, registration in the ITBMS taxpayer registry. A PIF with only foreign-source income and no Panamanian taxable operations is generally not required to obtain an RUC unless it imports, carries out taxable activities, or is selected as an electronic billing taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box system exists in Panama. A PIF may elect in its foundation deed to adopt specific governance, distribution, and investment provisions, but tax classification is fixed by the Tax Code: entity-level taxation solely on Panama-source income; foreign-source income is outside Panamanian territorial scope. No hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (VAT-style transfer tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 36,000 (Panama Balboa, at parity with USD) in annual gross taxable sales; however, importers of goods are captured on the first taxable import, and the DGI may require registration for taxpayers below the threshold in specific circumstances.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The DGI has a compulsory electronic invoicing regime. Selected taxpayers, including large taxpayers and others meeting DGI turnover criteria, must issue invoices through DGI-certified software or the Sede Electrónica, transmit invoice data electronically in real time to the DGI, and obtain a DGI authorization number. Export invoices must reference the customs export declaration. There is no physical digital stamp; control is exercised through DGI validation and real-time clearance of the electronic invoice via the approved web-service/API channel.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to tangible goods, including all-terrain military tactical vehicles, physically exported from Panama, and to services supplied to non-resident recipients for use wholly abroad, provided title and risk pass outside Panamanian customs territory. The taxpayer must demonstrate actual physical exit, delivery under a government-to-government or diplomatic contract where applicable, and receipt of payment from the non-resident buyer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera, DUA)
Bill of Lading or Airwaybill showing Panamanian departure and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate from a Panamanian licensed bank evidencing foreign-currency repatriation
Commercial invoice and packing list corresponding exactly to the customs declaration
Certificate of Origin or end-user/government purchase order for defense procurement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas may jointly audit export transactions; a failure to produce the required export/remittance bundle, or a fraudulent zero-rating claim, triggers retrospective ITBMS assessment at the standard 7% rate, plus statutory interest, administrative fines up to 100% of the omitted tax, and criminal liability for tax fraud, customs fraud, or false documentation under Panamanian law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No national central bank; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) supervises the banking system, and Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent; monetary policy is effectively delegated to the United States Federal Reserve through full dollarization with the Panamanian balboa pegged 1:1 to the USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama applies a fully dollarized monetary system with unrestricted convertibility of both capital and current account flows. The Panamanian balboa is a non-issued unit defined at par with the U.S. dollar, and all bank liabilities and settlements are denominated in USD. There are no exchange-control restrictions on dividend distributions, profit remittance, capital repatriation, or intercompany loans. Operational constraints arise only from AML/KYC banking due diligence, tax compliance under Panama's territorial tax rules, and the need to maintain settlement accounts at SBP-licensed institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists. There are no mandatory conversion ratios, prescribed deposit windows, or central-bank repatriation deadlines for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in USD in any Panamanian commercial bank or authorized foreign correspondent account, provided the bank receives the underlying commercial invoice, export clearance documentation, and, where applicable, ministry license or end-user certificate for regulated defense goods.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and USD Clearing Hub
Capital Escrow Account; Government Receivable Account
Operational Account and Foreign Trade Settlement
Operational Account with FX Derivative Access
Capital Escrow Account for Private Interest Foundation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low (restricted). Offshore fintech EMI providers cannot hold a Panamanian deposit account or act as an exclusive treasury rail without an SBP banking authorization; they may serve only as a supplementary payment channel for staff expenses and limited working-capital disbursements. For defense manufacturing, government direct wires, diplomatic letters of credit, and high-value trade settlements require a fully licensed Panamanian commercial bank account with correspondent banking through the United States. EMI transactions also risk causing negative OCR scrutiny and refusal of documentary LCs. A practical onboarding approach is to use the EMI solely as a lower-tier sub-account for procurement not exceeding USD 50,000 while preserving the licensed bank account as the prime legal clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical appearance for high-risk defense-sector appointments. At least one founder, director, or authorized officer holding a notarized power of attorney must appear in person before a Panamanian notary or, where Panama has no consular presence, before a notary in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction with apostille verification. Remote opening is permissible for entities with lower AML risk profiles, but for manufacturing of armored tactical vehicles, SBP-flavored EDD policies require a direct senior-compliance interview in Spanish or English, either physically or by simultaneous video link, with independent identity verification of the UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expiry or absence of a statutory license for manufacturing military-grade armored vehicles and defense components.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of valid arms and munitions manufacturing authorization issued by the current Panamanian competent authority (Ministerio de Seguridad Pública or its designee), together with the corporate registry excerpt evidencing that ISIC 3040 is within the foundation's licensed scope, and a signed declaration that final sales are restricted to approved state or diplomatic end users.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity of the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) and inability to reconstruct the ultimate human owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified foundation deed from Registro Público de Panamá; full register of foundation council members and protectors; current beneficial ownership declaration filed with the Dirección General de Ingresos under Ley 129 de 2020; a personal identification statement from the founder/final UBO; and a sworn certificate of good standing issued within the previous 90 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic concentration risk when the PIF receives or disburses funds to sanctioned or conflict-affected jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level geographic risk matrix; live OFAC and UN sanctions screening reports; evidence that the PIF maintains an internal PEP/sanctions filter; contractual end-user and anti-transshipment clauses; and shipping route confirmation from an acceptable maritime registry or cargo surveyor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient audited banking trail and unexplained lump-sum capital injections from private foundations in tax-haven countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the past three years; MT103 histories for all inbound USD transfers; certified capital contribution resolutions; signed source-of-funds statement referencing the military-commerce contract; and a capital escrow account acknowledgment issued by Banco Nacional de Panamá.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections execute as SWIFT MT103 messages to the SBP-licensed bank's U.S. correspondent shell and then participate in Panama's local automated clearing house. The remitter must use full legal name PA_PIF, address in the Republic of Panama, the foundation registration number, and a purpose code aligned with BPM6 'Direct Investment Equity Capital Injection'. Because Panama imposes no FX approvals, only threshold AML reporting applies; for amounts exceeding USD 250,000 the beneficiary bank may request a route-of-funds memorandum, the resolved public registry, an escrow balance statement, and a copy of the underlying military procurement contract or government order. The preferred inbound protocol is an escrow to protected capital account with BNP, then a SWIFT-confirmed transfer to Banco General when conditions are met.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for fixed-fee supplier invoices and commercial LC (MT700/MT707) for diplomatic or government procurement contracts. Panamanian banks issue LC documentary settlements under ICC UCP600, with the PIF as initiating applicant and a U.S. or EU confirming bank for unconfirmed political risks. Acceptable clearing rails include (i) outgoing SWIFT wire to suppliers, (ii) sight LC against packing list and transport document where shipment is by bonded carrier, and (iii) usance LC for 180-day diplomatic payment terms with title-retention clauses. For defense-material imports, the companion export license and final import certificate must accompany the full e-bank document set, and the receiving bank must maintain an OFAC-taught screen and UN sanction filter on each payment instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR vanilla forward contracts up to 24 months against documented European component purchase orders
USD/CNH non-deliverable forward contracts for Chinese steel and electronics supply transactions
USD/MXN and USD/COP dynamic forwards or non-deliverable forwards for regional raw-material procurement
USD/EUR cross-currency swaps matched to the PIF's euro-denominated receivables from embassy or diplomatic purchasing programs
Structured FX forwards with an embedded knockout option, limited to the exact notional of confirmed purchase orders and subject to senior credit approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payment of the Private Interest Foundation annual government maintenance fee (Tasa Única) and issuance of the DGI good-standing clearance (Certificado de Paz y Salvo)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama; remitted through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March (calendar-year, first-quarter statutory payment window)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment recargo of 10% of the fee (minimum USD 100) after 31 March; DGI will withhold the Paz y Salvo certificate; two consecutive years of non-payment trigger administrative strike-off proceedings by the Registro Público and loss of the foundation's legal capacity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración de Renta) and delivery of audited financial statements where the foundation derives Panamanian-source taxable income; dormant foundations holding foreign or passive assets are outside the scope of the territorial income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Panama (electronic filing via T@-DGI / Formulario 100)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within three months after the 31 December fiscal year-end, due by 31 March; also required upon liquidation or change of taxable status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines under the Fiscal Code, monthly punitive interest on unpaid tax at 1.5%, DGI presumptive-assessment authority for non-filers, and suspension of good-standing certification until the return and payment are settled

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO/AML compliance attestation and resident-agent KYC refresh confirming the founder, Foundation Council members, beneficiaries, and protector as of the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Resident Agent maintaining the confidential beneficial-ownership register; disclosure to DGI, the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), or the Public Prosecutor only upon lawful AML/CFT request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the foundation registration anniversary and upon any transfer of beneficial interests or amendment of the foundation charter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil and administrative fines and criminal liability under Law 23 of 2015 and Law 52 of 2013 for false, incomplete, or outdated UBO records; resident-agent license suspension; enhanced defense-sector (ISIC 3040) scrutiny and denial of banking and government/diplomatic payment rails

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance of the registered office and resident-agent designation, including recording of foundation amendments and Foundation Council resolutions in the Registro Público and the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panama (Public Registry) whenever the resident agent, registered office, charter, or council composition changes; otherwise maintained in the agent's compliance file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the office/agent attestation; notarial registration within the statutory period following any charter or agent change (anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed resident agent is grounds for administrative dissolution; outdated registry particulars invalidate the good-standing certificate and block counterparty onboarding with government, defense, and diplomatic clients

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: DGI mandates an independent audit by a Panamanian Certified Public Accountant when gross annual income subject to Panamanian-source taxation exceeds B/.250,000 (USD 250,000) under Executive Decree No. 170 of 1993; the DGI may also order audits for lower-income taxpayers in high-risk sectors; defense procurement counterparties frequently impose contractually audited IFRS statements regardless of statutory exemption
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted by the National Financial Accounting Standards Commission (CNCF); small and medium entities may apply IFRS for SMEs; audited statements must be presented in Spanish and accompany the DGI annual return when the audit threshold is met

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 52 of 2013 and Executive Decree No. 35 of 2015 require the foundation to maintain an updated, confidential beneficial-ownership register at the resident agent's office. The resident agent performs an annual KYC/UBO confirmation of the founder, Foundation Council members, beneficiaries, and protector, and any transfer of beneficial interests must be evidenced by notarial deed, Foundation Council resolution, and registry annotation. UBO information is disclosed exclusively to competent authorities on lawful request; non-compliance exposes the foundation and the resident agent to AML/CFT penalties under Law 23 of 2015 and enhanced due-diligence consequences in the defense industry
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registro de Beneficiarios de la Fundación)
Register of Directors (Registro de Miembros del Consejo de la Fundación)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600 - US$1,200 per annum (licensed resident agent and registered office in Panama City)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500 - US$7,500 per engagement (IFRS audit by a Panamanian CPA; dormant PIFs without Panamanian-source income are ordinarily below the compulsory-audit threshold)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives are territorial in nature: a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation is subject to corporate income tax only on Panama-source income, while genuine foreign-source income and gains remain outside the net of the 25% corporate tax. There is no automatic CIT holiday for ISIC 3040 armored military tactical vehicle manufacturing; a qualifying operator in a designated special economic zone or under Panama's Multinational Headquarters Law may obtain specific preferential treatment. Dividend distributions out of earnings already subjected to the 25% corporate income tax benefit from a reduced dividend withholding tax rate of 5%, rather than the general statutory 10%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1935 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through the DGI Sede Electrónica portal at sede.dgi.gob.pa using the entity's RUC and DGI registration. A Private Interest Foundation engaged in Panamanian-source commercial activity must be registered with the Dirección General de Impuestos and represented by its licensed resident agent or designated fiscal representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; monthly or quarterly advance income tax payments are required where the taxpayer's Panamanian-source taxable income exceeds the statutory thresholds under the Panama Tax Code.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before March 15 of the year following the calendar tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; taxpayers with an approved non-calendar fiscal year must file no later than the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: full legal name, RUC, fiscal year-end, ISIC/NAICS economic activity code (3040 / 336992), commercial registry and foundation deed details, registered address, and resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs must identify the Panamanian resident agent and DGI-authorized fiscal representative; attach the public deed of foundation and valid annual franchise tax payment evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Panamanian-source gross receipts: includes manufacturing revenue, sale of armored all-terrain tactical vehicles, spares, maintenance contracts, and any remittances that Panama's territorial sourcing rules treat as Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include income derived from activities performed, assets located, or contracts executed in Panama; do not include unrelated foreign-source passive income of the PIF where territorial rules exclude it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and cost of goods sold: production material, direct labor, depreciation, factory overhead, R&D, professional fees, royalties, interest, taxes, and ordinary operating expenses attributable to Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be supported by invoices, customs forms, transfer pricing documentation, bank records, and statutory accounting books; expenses allocated to foreign-source income are nondeductible against Panama-source profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after loss carryforward: Panama-source gross receipts minus allowable deductions, adjusted for transfer pricing and prior-year losses within the 5-year limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF may not offset foreign losses against Panamanian-source taxable income unless a clear statutory nexus exists; the loss carryforward certificate must be maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computation at the 25% statutory corporate rate, including the applicable alternative minimum tax or other final withholding tax regimes, and any statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers whose only Panama-source income is subject to final withholding have no further Box 5 liability; where a local manufacturing plant exists, full 25% corporation tax applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance due or refund: offset advance payments, ITBMS withholdings, tax credits, and any payments made under DTA reservations; final balance payable at filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds require audited financial statements, tax residence certificate, and complete source documentation; non-residents must maintain a Panamanian fiscal address for refund processing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers a DGI-assessed surcharge of 1% per month or fraction on the unpaid tax, up to 20%, plus managerial fines; false or incomplete returns attract penalties of 25%-100% of the omitted tax, and criminal tax evasion sanctions under the Panama Penal Code may be invoked.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory dividend withholding tax is 10%; when dividends are paid from profits that have already been subject to Panama corporate income tax at the ordinary 25% rate, the effective withholding rate is reduced to 5% as a credit mechanism.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Panama-recognized Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction's tax authority, establish beneficial ownership, and provide the certificate to the Panamanian payor before or at distribution. The payor must retain the TRC, ownership chain documentation, and DTA-specific forms for at least five years; where treaty relief cannot be applied at source, the non-resident may file a refund claim with DGI within the statutory claim period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for use of intellectual property in Panama are subject to 10% statutory withholding tax on gross Panamanian-source payments. Interest paid on Panamanian-source credit obligations is generally subject to 5% withholding tax, except for qualifying international banking transactions or where DTA relief applies; treaty rates under Panama's DTAs typically range from 0%-10% for interest and 5%-10% for royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File documentation is triggered when Panamanian-source gross operating revenue exceeds B/.2,000,000 (US$2,000,000) or when related-party transactions collectively exceed B/.250,000 (US$250,000). A sworn transfer pricing disclosure must accompany Form 1935, and documentation must be available to DGI within the statutory administrative period.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Ley 21 de 2019 and implementing executive decrees) require economic presence and substance for relevant activities carried out by Panamanian entities. An ISIC 3040 armored tactical vehicle manufacturer with an active plant in Panama is an operational commercial business and generally satisfies the substance standard by maintaining Panamanian premises, local workforce, board/council meetings, accounting records, and core income-generating decisions in Panama. A PIF used merely as a passive holder of foreign military-linked assets must demonstrate adequate local substance or risk losing territorial tax benefits and incurring ESR penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Omission of Panama-Source Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting Panama-source manufacturing receipts, fabricating export invoices, recording personal expenses as defense contract costs, using undisclosed foreign accounts for local vehicle sales, or failing to file Form 1935 while deriving income from Panamanian factory activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI summarily reassesses the omitted tax, imposes a monthly surcharge of 1% up to 20%, civil penalties of 25%-100% of the evaded tax, and assessment interest; criminal conviction for tax evasion may result in imprisonment of 2 to 5 years plus a fine up to twice the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and council members who sign false declarations are jointly liable for civil restitution; Panama courts can pierce the foundation's veil upon proof of alter ego or asset commingling, exposing personal assets. Criminal proceedings may result in travel bans, asset embargoes, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Foundation / Artificial Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF without real administrative functions in Panama, using nominee council members with no authority, failing to maintain accounting records, not paying the annual foundation franchise fee, or treating active defense manufacturing revenue as foreign-source while management and production are effectively controlled abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI or the Registrar may strike off or dissolve the PIF, cancel the registered agent license, deny territorial tax exemptions, impose ESR penalties up to substantial administrative fines, and assess all Panamanian-source tax at 25% plus surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Founders, council members, and protectors who permit shell operation are liable for fraudulent transfers and civil restitution; Panamanian courts may disregard the foundation's separate legal personality and attach the personal assets of those who directed the sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Defense Export Licensing / AML Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manufacturing or exporting all-terrain military tactical vehicles without the required defense-related license, transacting with unauthorized end-users, using hidden beneficial ownership through the PIF to evade export controls, or accepting structured cash payments to avoid AML reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Special licenses are revoked; authorities may seize vehicles and production equipment; AML sanctions under Panama Law 23 of 2015 include fines up to B/.1,000,000 and criminal money-laundering penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment plus forfeiture of proceeds; defense export violations may trigger additional separate fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers carry statutory AML obligations to identify beneficial owners and monitor high-risk defense transactions. Willful blindness creates personal criminal exposure, travel bans, Interpol alerts, and civil liability for financing of unauthorized military transfers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party procurement of military components, shared IP licensing, management fees, or intercompany sales of tactical vehicles priced outside arm's length; failing to prepare the Local File, Master File, or comparability study after the statutory thresholds are exceeded; providing false or incomplete TP disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may make arm's-length adjustments increasing Panamanian-source taxable income, impose compensatory interest on underpaid tax, apply surcharges, and levy fines for defective documentation; deliberate concealment escalates the matter to criminal tax fraud prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false transfer pricing documentation or instruct related-party invoicing outside arm's length are jointly liable for additional taxes and penalties; in fraud cases, courts may pierce the corporate/foundation veil and impose personal restitution, travel restrictions, and imprisonment.
